text: At the time of the events giving rise to the application, Hyde Park (the first applicant) was registered with the Moldovan Ministry of Justice as a non-governmental organisation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) lobbied, among other things, for freedom of expression and the right to peaceful assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In 2007, Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue the organisation's registration with the Moldovan Ministry of Justice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members decided to discontinue the organisation's registration on grounds of alleged pressure and intimidation by the State.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the refusal of the Moldovan Ministry of Justice to register amendments to Hyde Park's articles of association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the repeated freezing of Hyde Park's bank account.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of the arbitrary arrest of Hyde Park's members.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park's members complained of attempts to shut down Hyde Park's newspaper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Several of Hyde Park's leaders requested political asylum in western countries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: It was decided to continue Hyde Park's activity under the same name but without registering it with the State authorities.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: It was decided that the new unincorporated association would become the former registered organisation's successor.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park was removed from the Government's list of non-governmental organisations on 2 June 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: After removal from the Government's list of non-governmental organisations on 2 June 2008, Hyde Park's activities continued as before on the basis of its new articles of association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the unincorporated association) continued editing its newspaper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the unincorporated association) continued editing its Internet page.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the unincorporated association) continued staging protests and demonstrations.

text: On 26 September 2005, Hyde Park (the first applicant) applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful rally in the Stefan cel Mare Park in Chişinău.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The peaceful rally for which Hyde Park sought authorisation was planned for 14 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The peaceful rally for which Hyde Park sought authorisation was in support of freedom of speech.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 October 2005, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application to hold a rally in the Stefan cel Mare Park on 14 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application on the ground that on 14 October 2005 a number of events were planned in the city centre, including in the Stefan cel Mare Park.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application on the ground that 14 October 2005 was a day of public holiday.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council's decision rejecting Hyde Park's application was sent by mail to Hyde Park on 10 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council's decision rejecting Hyde Park's application was received by Hyde Park on 12 October 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 12 October 2005, Hyde Park (the first applicant) challenged the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the rally in court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) argued, among other things, that the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal was unlawful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) argued that the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal was contrary to Article 11 of the Convention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) asked that the case be examined urgently.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 2 December 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action challenging the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the rally.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the Chişinău Municipal Council had lawfully rejected Hyde Park's application to hold a rally.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal considered that since other events were scheduled to take place in the Stefan cel Mare Park on 14 October 2005, such as exhibitions, sports events, concerts and other demonstrations, Hyde Park's rally might hinder those events.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal considered that Hyde Park's rally might endanger public order.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal noted that the application to the Chişinău Municipal Council had been signed by the president of Hyde Park.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal noted that there was no evidence in the case file that the council of Hyde Park had approved the application to hold the rally.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park appealed against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 2 December 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park argued on appeal that the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment breached its members' right to freedom of assembly as guaranteed by Article 11 of the Convention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park argued on appeal that the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment was contrary to the provisions of the Assemblies Act.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Hyde Park argued on appeal that there was no evidence that the rally would endanger public order.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 May 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed Hyde Park's (the first applicant's) appeal on points of law against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice reiterated that authorising Hyde Park's rally at the same time as other cultural and sports demonstrations in the Stefan cel Mare Park ran the risk of resulting in violent clashes and thus endangered public order.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in the following circumstances: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of the public authorities, the local authorities, prosecutors' offices, the courts or companies with armed security.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the parliament building, the residence of the president of Moldova, the seat of the government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.
Section 8(4) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that free access to the premises of the institutions listed in Section 8(3) shall be guaranteed.
Section 8(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local public authorities may, if the organisers agree, establish places or buildings for permanent assemblies.

Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council, a specimen of which is set out in the annex which forms an integral part of the Act.

Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate: the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly; the date, starting time and finishing time of the assembly; the location of the assembly and the access and return routes; the manner in which the assembly is to take place; the approximate number of participants; the persons who are to ensure and answer for the sound conduct of the assembly; and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.

Section 11(3) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that if the situation so requires, the Municipal Council may alter certain aspects of the prior notification with the agreement of the organiser of the assembly.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest five days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that when the prior notification is considered at an ordinary or extraordinary meeting of the Municipal Council, the discussion shall deal with the form, timetable, location and other conditions for the conduct of the assembly and the decision taken shall take account of the specific situation.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, they have obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of Sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge in the administrative courts the refusal of the local government.
